comments.body: @jackfromeast Could you please use the crash template when you open your issues instead of the blank one please?

Hum. The question I ask myself is: should we continue making it grow or not? we are actually building an array of Tcl_Obj, but we pre-compute the list's size so we have some solutions:

- Copy the content of the list in an internal tuple and use the tuple from there. I can optimize this path for exact lists or tuples that are known to be safe, but otherwise I'll need to call `tuple(object)` first and work on that tuple.
- Resize the allocated array when needed. It's a bit more flexible and only requires C resizes and size checks.
- Only use whatever I could copy, e.g., if we call clear() in the middle, then just copy the initial objects. Or, if the list object changes its size during iteration and we get an index out of bound, the just raise that IndexError. If the list grows, don't copy past what we already knew. And if the list is mutated, use the "old" item value that was inserted.

The easiest for me would be to copy the content of the list into a temporary tuple and work with it.

@serhiy-storchaka what are your thoughts on this one?

Without tkinter involved:
```
victim = []

class Evil:
    def __str__(self):
        victim.clear()
        return "boom"

victim[:] = ['before', Evil(), 'after']
for s in victim: print(s)
```
prints
```
before
boom
```
Replacing the last line with
```
result = [s for s in victim]
print(result)
```
seems more line the OP's code.  It changes the result to `['before', <__main__.Evil object at 0x000001D43FCD9A90>, 'after']`.  I am not sure why the difference, but I expect a tuple copy would result in something equivalent.
I think, I'll go for a tuple copy but only if we don't provide an exact list or tuple. Most of the time, people will just use plain lists or tuples and not their custom sequences.

I knew about this bug as soon as I committed list support. It just looked too insignificant and was too low on my priority list. But if it has been discovered by third party, there is no reason to not fix it.

It does not matter how you fix it. You convert all list elements to Tcl objects, so making an intermediate tuple copy (which will just create new references) will not make a difference.
